Run submission, retries and accepted work

html:
Workflow browser, editor and submission flows

The Workflow browser saves reviewed requests and submits explicit run or schedule intent. Its editor draft, the saved definition revision and an accepted task are separate states. workflows.js owns the shared browser controller. Workflow definitions, invocation and recovery owns server validation, copied assets, claims, current model routing and recovery. Workflows — saved requests describes the human controls.

Entry points and data ownership

flowchart TD Draft[Unsent Chat draft] --> Editor[Reusable Workflow editor] Turn[Historical user prompt] --> Editor Cards[Library cards] --> Editor Editor --> Preview[Candidate, draft or revision context preview] Preview --> Fields[Exact prompt, settings and optional context choices] Fields --> Save[Explicit create or revision-checked update] Save --> Routes[Recipe routes] Routes --> Definitions[Definition revisions and owned context assets] Cards --> Run[Run now: reviewed revision and submission key] Run --> Routes Routes --> Task[Ordinary durable task with current model routing] Task --> Conversation[Run conversation and task history] Cards --> Schedule[Shared schedule editor] Schedule --> Binding[Recipe revision and timing intent] Binding --> Routes Routes --> Event[Existing event scheduler]

Desktop Chat supplies the current prompt, conversation identity, attachment references and settings through its configuration callback. The mobile adapter supplies the same draft shape using mobile submission settings. Reading that callback does not send or clear the composer. Existing turn actions prefer the persisted request ID; an unpersisted turn instead supplies a draft copy. The controller hides save actions for non-user-authored or slash-command text.

The library page supplies the list, search, sort and error hosts in workflows.html. Calling library() elsewhere navigates to /workflows. On that page, startup loads inventory before focusing an optional ?workflow= card. There is no background interval poll: broker changes request fresh inventory.

configure() replaces the controller options object. Desktop also supplies an accepted-run callback to open the new conversation; the library and mobile default to navigation. Exported methods share one page-lived dialog and cached inventory. The context and schedule options supplied by desktop are not read by this controller; scheduling uses SMTOScheduleEditor directly.

Editor reads and explicit writes

Opening any editor, history or confirmation replaces the dialog's generation and disposes its read view. Closing it advances the generation again and restores the original focus target if still connected. This cancels owned preview/history reads and suppresses obsolete painting. Save and delete requests use independent writes; closing a dialog does not cancel an already accepted server change.

sequenceDiagram actor U as Human participant E as Shared editor participant V as Owned read view participant R as Recipe routes U->>E: Open historical source, draft or saved definition E->>V: Replace generation and own read signal alt Historical source E->>R: GET source candidate with read signal R-->>E: Prompt, settings, context and completeness else New or unsent draft E->>R: GET defaults as needed E->>R: POST draft-preview with read signal R-->>E: Normalized settings and available context else Existing definition E->>R: GET context-preview for displayed revision R-->>E: Revision context summary end E->>E: Paint only if read view is current and dialog open U->>E: Review exact prompt, inclusion switches and settings opt Historical settings incomplete U->>E: Choose Use current settings E->>R: GET defaults R-->>E: Current supported settings E->>E: Adopt only in the same open generation end U->>E: Save E->>R: POST create or PATCH with expected_revision alt Rejected or unconfirmed R-->>E: Error E-->>U: Keep draft and show error if still current else Acknowledged R-->>E: Saved definition E->>E: Check generation before changing dialog E-->>U: Refresh library or show saved link end Note over E,R: A later closed dialog or failed refresh does not roll back a write

A historical source reads its candidate settings/context. A new draft asks the server for a preview using conversation identity, settings and attachment references. Editing a saved definition reads context for its displayed revision. The preview POST computes review data; it does not create a definition or launch a model. Unavailable context is shown separately from a known empty category. The server owns extraction boundaries and the eventual copy into Workflow-owned assets.

The prompt remains exact editable text, with a UTF-8 byte count independent of optional context. New saves start all three inclusion switches off; editing retains the stored choices. Source context stops before that request's own answer and tool results. Choosing Use current settings is explicit and generation-checked; its request itself is not cancelled by the read-view signal.

Advanced settings are parsed as JSON at save time and validated by the server. Changing the Gateway text field from the loaded snapshot removes gateway_selection and supplies the typed single gateway_id. Leaving that field unchanged preserves the advanced JSON selection. A nonempty working-directory field overrides terminal_cwd; blanking the field does not remove a value already present in JSON. The browser does not infer that an empty control resets the saved configuration.

Each save disables its own button until settlement. Create sends the source request or draft conversation/attachment identities and explicit current-settings choice. Edit sends expected_revision. A stale revision remains an error for the human to resolve; the browser does not silently overwrite or automatically reload the draft. Successful library saves close the editor and reload cards. Chat saves show a link without modifying the composer. A late acknowledgement for a replaced/closed dialog is ignored for presentation, even though the server may have accepted the write.

Run submission, retries and accepted work

sequenceDiagram actor U as Human participant B as Original Run button participant W as Workflow controller participant R as Recipe routes participant T as Existing task owner U->>B: Run now B->>W: Displayed recipe and revision W->>W: Reject duplicate in-flight launch for this recipe W->>B: Keep or create submission key on this element W->>R: POST execute with revision and key R->>R: Validate request and resolve claim opt Accepted or existing submission R->>T: Create or resolve the ordinary task end alt Response rejected or unconfirmed R-->>W: Error W-->>U: Show page error and release busy state Note over B,W: Original button keeps its key for a retry else Successful acknowledgement R-->>W: Run and conversation identities W->>B: Remove retained key W-->>U: Open accepted run conversation Note over R,T: Task completion is observed through normal task surfaces end

A per-recipe set blocks overlapping browser launches while the request and accepted-run callback are pending. The server separately enforces claims and prevents overlapping open runs. The submission key is retained on the originating button after an API error and cleared immediately after a successful response, before navigation or the caller's callback. A callback/navigation problem after that response does not undo task acceptance.

This is element-local retry state. A library rebuild replaces buttons, and a page reload also loses the key. A later click on a replacement button can therefore use a new key. The browser does not persist uncertain submissions across redraws or automatically replay a failed POST. Inspect History and the run conversation when acceptance is uncertain. The API's stable-key retry guarantee is described in manual invocation.

Library invalidation, history and deletion

flowchart TD Init[Initial load or explicit refresh] --> Pending{Read pending?} Broker[Recipes, tasks or runs changed] --> Pending Pending -->|Yes| Dirty[Mark trailing read] Dirty --> Wait[Await shared read chain] Pending -->|No| Begin[Clear dirty flag] Begin --> Fetch[GET recipes] Fetch -->|Success| Publish[Cache list and render] Publish --> Again{Dirty flag set?} Again -->|Yes| Begin Again -->|No| Done[Release pending read] Fetch -->|Failure| Done Done --> Feedback[Settle refresh caller] Wait --> Feedback

Concurrent refresh callers share one read chain and mark it dirty for a trailing iteration. Each successful response may paint before the trailing fetch; this is coalescing, not a rule that discards every pre-invalidation response. Search matches cached titles and prompts case-insensitively. Sort uses title or update time. Cards are rebuilt rather than patched in place, which explains the Run-key limit. Focus returns to the same card/action when possible, or to New workflow if the focused card disappeared. Mutation-owned busy feedback can span the write and its follow-up inventory read; the caller finishes that feedback.

History uses the owned read view, then displays revision identities, run statuses, errors and conversation links as text. It does not replay steps or submit another run. Delete opens an explicit confirmation. After its DELETE acknowledgement it refreshes inventory, closing the confirmation only if the same generation is still active. The client does not send a revision precondition for delete. The server's retained revisions/tasks/schedules remain governed by the definition lifecycle. A failed post-write inventory refresh is separate from the accepted deletion.

Schedule binding

sequenceDiagram actor U as Human participant W as Workflow card participant E as Shared schedule editor participant R as Recipe routes participant S as Existing scheduler U->>W: Schedule displayed revision W->>E: Open with saved title, prompt and settings U->>E: Review timing and notification choices E->>W: Save callback with schedule fields W->>R: POST schedule with recipe_revision R->>R: Validate and bind the saved revision R->>S: Create ordinary scheduled Agent event S-->>R: Stored event R-->>E: Save result through callback Note over R,S: Later definition edits do not change this pinned binding

The callback forwards only schedule type, interval, next-run time, timezone, recurrence and notification choices. It supplies the saved title/prompt and agent_prompt action itself. The Recipe routes validate that intent and pin the revision; the browser does not run a timer or independently execute the Workflow. Timing calculations and schedule editing belong to scheduled events.

Review boundary

The shared browser module was reviewed in full. Desktop/mobile draft adapters and library element wiring were inspected only at the boundaries described here. The server contracts retain their separate source review in guide 54. Browser checks use isolated local state and scripted model/Gateway fixtures; they do not validate a live model or remote installation. Theme, tooltip and appearance implementation are outside this documentation pass.
